opinion.label: Opinion
keywords: business architecture pain points versus root cause
opinion.curatorPrompt: Include pieces that discuss Business Architecture (capability mapping, value stream design, role/actor modeling, cross-mapping, BIZBOK practice) where the article also engages with structural weaknesses, blind spots, or limitations of static mapping approaches -- especially anything on design-time versus post-hoc detection of organisational problems. Favour Business Architecture Guild content, BIZBOK-adjacent practitioner writing, enterprise/business architecture trade press, and organisational psychology sources on role conflict or role strain (e.g. Kahn-lineage literature) where they connect to organisational design rather than pure individual wellbeing framing. Exclude generic digital transformation hype, agentic AI pieces with no structural design angle, and UX/product friction content (different domain). Flag borderline pieces that discuss role ambiguity, accountability conflict, or capability gaps without an explicit design-time framing -- these may still be relevant to a design-time predictive claim.

caseStudy.label: Case Study
keywords: capability heat map case study outcome
role conflict organizational redesign case study
business architecture transformation case study outcome
capability cross mapping case study bank
operating model redesign case study financial services
value stream mapping transformation case study
org design role clarity case study outcome
business architecture maturity assessment case study
shared services role conflict case study
enterprise architecture governance case study outcome
caseStudy.curatorPrompt: Include case studies where a named or clearly described organisation applied Business Architecture artifacts (capability maps, value streams, RACI/role matrices, cross-maps) and the writeup describes a concrete structural outcome -- a fault line found, a role conflict resolved, a redesign driven by a capability or accountability gap. Prefer cases with enough specificity to be citable (named institution, described mechanism, described outcome) over generic 'transformation success story' pieces. Exclude pure technology rollout case studies with no organisational design or role/capability angle, and exclude UX/product friction case studies.

matcherPrompt: Pair Opinion and Case Study articles that share a structural theme relevant to Business Architecture and Friction: role/actor modeling gaps, capability cross-mapping limitations, design-time versus post-hoc detection of organisational fault lines, or accountability/role conflict within capability or value-stream design. A strong pair should let a reader see the conceptual claim in the Opinion piece and a concrete instance of it in the Case Study piece.
